sections.markdown:
## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Be in shape to drive

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A20
A DWI conviction requires an SR22 insurance filing with DPS and maintenance of that insurance for 3 years from the eligibility date. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A20
Alcohol and other impairing drugs reduce judgment, visual functioning, color discrimination and response speed. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A20
The handbook says alcohol-related visual effects can include blurred or double vision, slower focusing and poorer judgments of distance, speed and movement. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A20
The handbook states that vision is affected at a BAC of 0.02 percent for drivers generally. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A20
The handbook warns that impairment begins with the first drink and advises against driving any vehicle after alcohol or impairing drugs. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A20
Do not let a friend or relative drive after drinking. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A20
BAC expresses alcohol as a percentage relative to the blood in the body. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A20
A driver can still be impaired and convicted of impaired driving with BAC below 0.08 percent. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A20
BAC of at least 0.08 percent may lead to license or driving-privilege revocation for at least 30 days and criminal penalties. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A20
A person under 21 can be arrested for alcohol impairment at a BAC of 0.02 percent. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A20
An alcohol-concentration test commonly uses breath, blood or urine to measure alcohol in the body. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A20
South Dakota implied consent requires compliance with a lawfully requested alcohol-content test when impaired driving is suspected. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A20
Refusing a BAC test can result in loss of the driver license for 1 year. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A20
The implied-consent law of the arresting state applies even when the driver’s license came from another state. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A20
The handbook’s general first-alcohol-conviction summary gives a possible $300-to-$1,000 fine plus court costs, 15 to 365 days in jail and license suspension or revocation of 90 to 365 days. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A20
For under-21 zero tolerance at BAC of at least 0.02 percent, the handbook lists a first offense as a Class 2 misdemeanor with a fine and 30-day license loss. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A20
For under-21 zero tolerance at BAC of at least 0.02 percent, a second or later offense is listed as a Class 2 misdemeanor with a fine and 180-day license loss. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A20
The DWI schedule for BAC of at least 0.08 percent lists a first offense as a Class 1 misdemeanor with a fine, up to 1 year in prison or both, plus at least 30 days of license loss. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A20
The DWI schedule lists a second offense as a Class 1 misdemeanor with a fine, up to 1 year in prison or both, plus at least 1 year of license loss. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A20
Driving without a license during the second-DWI license-loss period brings at least 3 days in county jail that cannot be suspended upon conviction. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A21
The third-DWI schedule classifies the offense as a Class 6 felony, punishable by a fine, up to 2 years in prison and at least 1 year of license loss after release. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A21
A conviction for unlicensed driving during the third-DWI license-loss period requires at least 10 days in county jail that cannot be suspended. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A21
A drinker can have a high BAC without obvious outward signs of drunkenness. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R24 | anchor: A21
The handbook says crash risk rises for such drivers at BAC of 0.05 percent or higher even if they hide visible drunkenness. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R25 | anchor: A21
As BAC rises, judgment and accurate traffic decisions become increasingly impaired. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

sections.heading: C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Be in shape to drive
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Be in shape to drive

FACT_ID: sec05-R26 | anchor: A21
The THINK roadside program began in 1979 through cooperation between South Dakota DPS and the transportation department to memorialize crash victims and warn about dangerous driving. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R27 | anchor: A21
The THINK program places a separate roadside post and sign near the state-highway right-of-way for each person killed in the crash. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R28 | anchor: A21
A THINK sign is removed when immediate family objects, its condition deteriorates or damage makes it unsatisfactory, or the highway segment is reconstructed to new standards. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R29 | anchor: A21
After a THINK sign is removed, replacement requires a request from immediate family, including when someone else removed the sign. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R30 | anchor: A21
Nonprescription medicines for headaches, colds, allergies or nerves may cause drowsiness and affect driving. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R31 | anchor: A21
Stimulant or diet pills may cause nervousness, dizziness, poor concentration or visual effects. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R32 | anchor: A21
Before driving after an over-the-counter drug, read its warnings and ask a doctor or pharmacist when unsure about safety or side effects. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R33 | anchor: A22
Some prescription medicines can impair reflexes, judgment, sight and alertness in ways resembling alcohol. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R34 | anchor: A22
The handbook’s prescription examples include antidepressants, pain relievers, sleep medicines and sedatives. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R35 | anchor: A22
Read prescription and packaging warnings before taking a medicine, and ask the doctor or pharmacist about driving-related side effects when uncertain. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R36 | anchor: A22
Illegal drugs may impair reflexes, judgment, sight and alertness in ways resembling alcohol. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R37 | anchor: A22
The handbook reports more driving mistakes, glare-adjustment difficulty and traffic-violation arrests among marijuana users than other drivers. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R38 | anchor: A22
Do not combine drinking with other drugs, because the combination may amplify alcohol’s effects or add separate impairing effects. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R39 | anchor: A22
Strong emotions can interfere with thinking, attention and information processing while driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R40 | anchor: A22
An angry or overly excited driver should wait off the road until calm, using a short walk if needed. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R41 | anchor: A22
A worried or upset driver should focus on driving and may choose to have someone else drive. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R42 | anchor: A22
Leaving extra trip time helps an impatient driver avoid speeding and other risky actions. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R43 | anchor: A22
Do not drive around lowered railway gates or try to beat a train. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R44 | anchor: A22
Even minor illness or discomfort can affect driving, so the handbook recommends another driver when a person feels unwell and needs transportation. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R45 | anchor: A22
The handbook describes epilepsy under medical control as generally not dangerous for driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R46 | anchor: A22
An insulin-using driver with diabetes should not drive when there is any risk of an insulin reaction, blackout, convulsion or shock. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R47 | anchor: A22
The handbook links that diabetes-related risk to skipped food or an incorrect insulin amount and suggests another driver while a doctor adjusts the dose. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R48 | anchor: A22
Drivers with diabetes should obtain regular eye checks for night blindness or other visual problems. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R49 | anchor: A22
The handbook advises against driving with the listed heart or circulation problems or a danger of blackout, fainting or heart attack, and says to ask the treating doctor whether a heart condition affects driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0022]
